# Retro `<YYYY-MM-DD>`

> Template for `tasks/retros/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`. The scrum-master agent reads
> this file as the structural source of truth and fills it in with values
> derived from the recent merged PRs, review artifacts, and the lessons log.
>
> **Required structure** (the linter equivalent — anything that breaks these
> rules should be treated as a bug in the agent prompt):
>
> 1. A `## Retro inputs` ledger appears first (T-1001), declaring the material
>    the rest of the retro rests on. Produced by `bin/retro-inputs.sh` and
>    pasted verbatim — do not hand-write it. Its canonical ids and statuses
>    (single source: `templates/prompt-blocks/retro-inputs.md`):
>    - input: cycle-window
>    - input: review-artifacts
>    - input: provenance
>    - input: specs
>    - input: run-telemetry
>    - input: previous-retro
>    - input: lessons
>    - input: pr-metadata
>    - input: interventions
>    - status: read
>    - status: empty
>    - status: unavailable
>    empty means the input was consulted and held nothing; unavailable means it could not be consulted at all. Never report one as the other.
>    `check-retro.sh` validates this section against a closed enum and fails
>    closed — see "What this mechanism does not deliver" in
>    `docs/specs/T-1001-retro-input-acquisition.md`: it confirms the ledger is
>    well-formed, never that a `read` status is true.
> 2. Top-level heading is exactly `# Retro <YYYY-MM-DD>`.
> 3. The five sections appear in this order, each anchored on its own
>    language-neutral marker (T-1010, single source:
>    `templates/prompt-blocks/retro-sections.md`) with an H2 heading
>    immediately after it. The heading text is free — write it in whatever
>    language and wording you like, with or without a parenthetical — because
>    the marker is the contract, never the heading string:
>    - `<!-- retro-section: keep -->`
>    - `<!-- retro-section: problem -->`
>    - `<!-- retro-section: try -->`
>    - `<!-- retro-section: traps -->`
>    - `<!-- retro-section: lessons -->`
>    If a section has no real content, keep the marker and its heading and
>    write `- (none)` as a single bullet — never delete the marker or the
>    heading.
>    The `traps` (loop-trap self-check) section is **mandatory and not
>    skippable** — it is the AI-attest reflection on the Comprehension Debt /
>    Cognitive Surrender traps (see `docs/loop-engineering/loop-traps.md`).
>    `check-retro.sh` enforces it precisely because it is the reflection most
>    tempting to skip.
> 4. Every bullet under the `lessons` section starts with `` `[common]` `` or
>    `` `[target-specific]` ``. No bare bullets allowed.
> 5. Every bullet under `keep` / `problem` / `try` cites a source (PR number,
>    `tasks/reviews/T-XXX.md`, `tasks/lessons.md` line range, etc.) so the
>    observation can be traced.
> 6. The agent never edits `tasks/lessons.md`. Lesson candidates are
>    proposed here for the human to merge.
>
> **Migrating an older retro** (one written before the marker contract, or
> hand-written outside this template): insert the five marker lines above,
> immediately before each of the five existing section headings, and change
> nothing else — the heading text, wording, and language stay exactly as
> written. `check-retro.sh` rejects a pre-migration retro with no markers at
> all (no dual acceptance of the old shape), but a marker is a pure,
> content-free addition, so migrating one costs nothing beyond inserting five
> lines.
>
> Delete this blockquote when the file is filled in.

# Retro `<YYYY-MM-DD>`

**Cycle scope**: the last `<N>` merged PRs
**Pull requests**: `#<a>`, `#<b>`, `#<c>`, ...
**Generated by**: scrum-master agent v0 (manual trigger)

`bin/retro-inputs.sh` prints the `## Retro inputs` heading below and its
ledger lines together — paste its output here verbatim, unedited, right after
that heading. Example shape shown below (a well-formed ledger: all nine
canonical ids, exactly once, each one of `read` / `empty` / `unavailable`).
This paragraph and everything above it stays OUTSIDE the `## Retro inputs`
section on purpose: `bin/check-retro.sh` validates that section as a closed
ledger and fails on any non-ledger prose inside it, so an explanation of the
mechanism cannot itself live inside the mechanism it explains.

<!-- retro-section: traps -->
## Loop-trap check

> The faster the loop runs, the more a human drifts from the code
> (Comprehension Debt) and abdicates judgment (Cognitive Surrender). This
> self-check exists to guard against that. **Not skippable**
> (`check-retro.sh` makes it mandatory). See `docs/loop-engineering/loop-traps.md`
> for the full rationale.
> **Answering mode (AI-attest, current practice)**: do not turn this into a
> question for a human to answer later — the agent writing the retro reads
> the raw artifacts (logs, diffs, files) itself and answers with its own
> judgment, escalating only the items it genuinely could not verify as
> "unverified — human judgment needed."
> **S4 citation / two-tier attest (optional)**: when this cycle has an S4
> drift report (`tasks/reviews/<task-id>-drift.md`), quote its cross-provider
> verdict; items that still could not be verified may be closed by the
> orchestrator's optional second-tier attest (`## Orchestrator attest` — a
> convention, not a required heading).

- **Comprehension debt**: what generated code did you not read, or only
  weakly understand, this cycle? Cite a source (PR / file). `- (none)` is
  allowed, but only if you can honestly say you read every diff.
- **Review criteria re-stated**: restate, in one or two sentences, the actual
  criterion you used to decide "this is mergeable" this cycle. "The AI /
  agent said so" is not a valid answer.
- **Unverified self-report**: what did an agent call "done" without evidence
  (tests / logs / QA / a Codex verdict) backing it up? If anything, route it
  to next cycle's Try or to gathering the missing evidence.

<!-- retro-section: lessons -->
## Lesson candidates

> The agent only **proposes** candidates here; it never writes to
> `tasks/lessons.md`.
> Labels are `[common]` (generic — applies outside this repository) or
> `[target-specific]` (specific to this repository). No bare, unlabelled
> bullets.
> **De-identify**: a lesson records only the recurring pattern and the reason
> it recurs — never incident-specific identifying detail. Source points at an
> artifact in this repository, or is n/a.
> This de-identification rule is an authoring-time discipline, not a
> detector: it does not find identifying detail that is already written down.
> **Model-change-cycle hint only (scaffolding audit)**: only on a cycle where
> the execution model changed since the previous one, list relaxation
> candidates (constraints in `agents/*.md` or bound in the loop-guard /
> contract yaml that exist to compensate for an older model's weakness) here
> as labelled candidates, or as issue proposals. If the audit ran and found
> no legitimate candidate, write `no scaffolding relaxation candidates` in
> `## Notes` instead (a genuine zero-candidate result — do not manufacture a
> weak one). On a cycle with no model change, add nothing here.

- `[common]` `<lesson — 1-3 lines>`
- `[target-specific]` `<lesson>`

## Notes

- `<anything that was skipped / warned about while generating this retro. e.g. "PR #9 has no matching review.md">`
- `<missing inputs / auth errors / review files that broke naming convention also go here>`
